sentences.en: Hello, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast whereby we talk through some of the big changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这个播客中，我们探讨20几岁时经历的一些重大变化与人生过渡，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Okay, this week, we're talking about narcissism and the narcissiSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，本周我们来聊聊自恋和自恋狂。

sentences.en: You know, what better week to kind of talk about this?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，还有什么比这周更适合来聊聊这个话题呢？

sentences.en: My ex-boyfriend popped up to me in case anyone was interested.
sentences.zh: 以防有人感兴趣，我的前男友突然来找我了。

sentences.en: So I was like, wow, that kind of reminds me of a topic I haven't covered yet.
sentences.zh: 所以我就想，哇，这让我想到了一个我还没涵盖过的主题。

sentences.en: What better way to kind of take some inspiration from my own life?
sentences.zh: 还有什么比从我自己的生活中汲取一些灵感更好的方式呢？

sentences.en: Let him know I'm still thinking about him.
sentences.zh: 让他知道我还在想着他。

sentences.en: No, all jokes aside.
sentences.zh: 开玩笑啦，说正经的。

sentences.en: I have really wanted to cover this for a while.
sentences.zh: 我其实很想讨论这个话题已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: I think it's a really interesting personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常有趣的人格障碍。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time on this show, we don't really discuss, I think,
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候在这个节目里，我们其实并不太讨论，我觉得，

sentences.en: clinical disorders or pathological disorders.
sentences.zh: 临床障碍或病理障碍。

sentences.en: It's more like a broader discussion of things with, I think, some tenuous links to psychology and kind of jumping into it.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一个更广泛的讨论，其中包含一些与心理学貌似有关的联系，然后一头扎进去。

sentences.en: But I really wanted to discuss the psychology of narcissism because I think that it's become a term used very frequently.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想探讨自恋背后的心理学，因为我觉得这个词已经被频繁使用了。

sentences.en: It's one of those crossovers between pop culture and psychology that we're seeing a lot more of these days.
sentences.zh: 这是我们现在越来越多看到的流行文化与心理学交融的例子之一。

sentences.en: Another example is like gaslighting.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子就像是“煤气灯操纵”（Gaslighting）。

sentences.en: People use that all the time.
sentences.zh: 人们总是用这个词。

sentences.en: Or saying that someone is a narcissist is obviously a pretty big one.
sentences.zh: 或者说某人是个自恋狂，这显然也是相当普遍的一个。

sentences.en: But I do think we all know someone who's a narcissiSt.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为我们都认识某一个自恋狂。

sentences.en: Just take a moment.
sentences.zh: 花点时间想想。

sentences.en: Think about the people in your life.
sentences.zh: 想想你生活中的那些人。

sentences.en: Maybe self-diagnose them.
sentences.zh: 也许可以给他们做个自我诊断。

sentences.en: Maybe you've even had thoughts that you are a narcissiSt.
sentences.zh: 也许你甚至有过自己也是个自恋狂的想法。

sentences.en: And if you have, no fear.
sentences.zh: 如果你有过，不用害怕。

sentences.en: Because that probably means that you're not, which we're going to discuss in this episode.
sentences.zh: 因为那可能意味着你并不是，我们将在本期节目中讨论这一点。

sentences.en: I think in your 20s, you are very likely to encounter kind of a new breed of person as our identities become more developed.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在20几岁的时候，随着我们的身份认同变得更加成熟，你非常有可能遇到一种全新类型的人。

sentences.en: Someone whose ego just seems a little bit too big for their boots to hold.
sentences.zh: 那种自我意识似乎过于膨胀，以至于他们那双靴子都快装不下了的人。

sentences.en: So if these people exist and we're likely to encounter them and, you know, in our 20s is probably the first time we really meet someone that's like this
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这样的人存在，而且我们很有可能会遇到他们，并且，你知道的，在我们20几岁的时候，这可能是我们第一次真正遇到这样的人，

sentences.en: and we're able to see that that's abnormal.
sentences.zh: 并且我们能够看出这是不正常的。

sentences.en: How do we have relationships with these people?
sentences.zh: 我们如何与这些人和谐相处？

sentences.en: How do we interact with them?
sentences.zh: 我们如何与他们互动？

sentences.en: How do we work with them?
sentences.zh: 我们如何与他们共事？

sentences.en: How do we date them?
sentences.zh: 我们如何与他们约会？

sentences.en: I also really wanted to explore some of the misconceptions around narcissism.
sentences.zh: 我还真的很想探讨一些关于自恋的误解。

sentences.en: Like I said, it is such a popularized term, but how often do we just use it quite flippantly without really knowing what it actually means
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这是一个非常大众化的词，但我们到底有多少次在不真正理解它实际含义的情况下，就轻率地使用它呢，

sentences.en: and whether someone actually is a narcissist, whether we can call them that.
sentences.zh: 以及某人是否真的是自恋狂，我们是否能这样称呼他们。

sentences.en: So we're going to discuss also some of the clinical implications of narcissism.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还将讨论自恋的一些临床意义。

sentences.en: So where does it come from?
sentences.zh: 那么它究竟从何而来？

sentences.en: This like discussion that it's in every corner of psychology is narcissism nature or nurture?
sentences.zh: 这种关于它充斥在心理学每一个角落的讨论，自恋究竟是先天决定的还是后天培养的？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a huge debate that's been raised for a long time and I don't think psychology is coming any closer to finding a real answer for that.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个长期存在的巨大争论，而且我认为心理学并没有更接近于找到这个问题的真正答案。

sentences.en: Another big question is, you know, does narcissism have a cure and should we deal with it?
sentences.zh: 另一个重大问题是，你知道的，自恋能治愈吗？我们是否应该把它当作一种精神障碍来处理，或者某种状况，而不是仅仅把它看作某人的性格缺陷？

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: There we go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Brief intermission.
sentences.zh: 短暂的幕间休息。

sentences.en: Bless me.
sentences.zh: 保佑我。

sentences.en: Anyhow, does narcissism have a cure and should we deal with it as a mental disorder, perhaps a condition, rather than just seeing it as maybe a fault of someone's character?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，自恋有治愈的方法吗？我们是否应该把它当作一种心理障碍，也许是一种状况来对待，而不是仅仅把它看作某人的性格缺陷？

sentences.en: Yeah, just some really big questions, but I think on a more personal note, we're going to discuss narcissism in our own lives, what it means for someone to be a narcissist,
sentences.zh: 是的，这只是一些非常重大的问题，但我觉得从更个人的层面来说，我们要讨论自己生活中的自恋，一个人成为自恋狂意味着什么，

sentences.en: how they operate, their behaviors, what it's like to date someone who's a narcissist, what it's like to be around people who are narcissists,
sentences.zh: 他们如何运作、他们的行为、和自恋狂约会是什么体验、身边都是自恋狂是什么感觉，

sentences.en: and how to kind of escape the manipulation and the charisma of a narcissiSt.
sentences.zh: 以及如何摆脱自恋狂的操控与个人魅力。

sentences.en: And don't worry, I do get the irony.
sentences.zh: 别担心，我明白这其中的讽刺意味。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of funny, like here I am, you know, making my own podcast, like listening to the sound of my voice and the episode is on narcissism, but maybe I'll, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这挺逗的，你看我，制作着自己的播客，听着自己声音的回响，而这一期的主题却是自恋，不过也许我……我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't think I'm a narcissist, but maybe someone will think I am after listening to some of these criteria.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得自己是个自恋狂，但也许听了其中某些标准后，会有人觉得我是。

sentences.en: So buckle in, because I've got a lot of energy today.
sentences.zh: 所以系好安全带，因为我今天能量满满。

sentences.en: Like I said, it's been a very complicated week and this is a topic I really want to dig into.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，这一周非常复杂，而这是一个我真的很想深入探讨的话题。

sentences.en: So let's do it.
sentences.zh: 那我们就开始吧。

sentences.en: So narcissism is extreme self-involvement to the degree that it makes a person ignore the needs of those around them.
sentences.zh: 所以，自恋是一种极端的自我沉迷，达到了让一个人忽视周围人需求的程度。

sentences.en: So while everyone, you know, may show occasional narcissistic behavior, because as my good friend Kate says, everyone is, you know, the center of their own universe.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然每个人，你知道的，都可能会表现出偶尔的自恋行为，因为正如我的好朋友凯特所说，每个人都是自己宇宙的中心。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that sometimes you have self-involvement, but true narcissists, they will frequently discard others' feelings and don't even seem to be aware of them.
sentences.zh: 所以有时会有自我沉迷也在情理之中，但真正的自恋狂，他们会频繁地无视他人的感受，甚至似乎完全没有意识到这些感受。

sentences.en: So they also just do not understand the effect that their behavior has on other people.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也不理解自己的行为对其他人产生的影响。

sentences.en: So they're unable to comprehend how their own self-involved behaviors have first and second order consequences.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们无法理解自己这种自我沉迷的行为所产生的第一层和第二层后果。

sentences.en: There are no, like, physical blood tests,
sentences.zh: 没有什么所谓的物理血液检测、

sentences.en: MRIs, GP appointments, or, you know, exact biological determinations that can identify a narcissiSt.
sentences.zh: 核磁共振、全科医生预约，或者说，你知道的，能够识别自恋狂的准确生物学测定。

sentences.en: Even therapists do just have to go on observations of the behavior and the attitude that a person presents.
sentences.zh: 即使是治疗师也只能根据一个人表现出的行为和态度来进行观察。

sentences.en: There's no, like, quiz.
sentences.zh: 没有什么所谓的测验。

sentences.en: Like, you might see people, like, posting things or, like, buzzfeed quizzes are like, are you a narcissist?
sentences.zh: 就像你可能会看到人们发布一些东西，或者像BuzzFeed那样的测验在问：你是自恋狂吗？

sentences.en: But that's not how it works.
sentences.zh: 但事情可不是这样的。

sentences.en: They basically have to just base what they're seeing in a person off of the DSM criteria.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上只能根据在一个人身上看到的情况，对照《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）的标准来进行判断。

sentences.en: And some of these criteria include
sentences.zh: 而这些标准包括了

sentences.en: superiority and entitlement, which we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 优越感和特权感，我们之前已经讨论过了。

sentences.en: So someone feeling like they deserve anything they would like and just go to any means to obtain that regardless of who they step on.
sentences.zh: 所以有人会觉得他们理应得到任何他们想要的东西，并且不惜一切代价去获得，哪怕踩着别人也在所不惜。

sentences.en: For a narcissist, like, there is no such thing as being wrong or feeling inferior.
sentences.zh: 对于自恋狂来说，根本没有“自己错了”或“感到低人一等”这回事。

sentences.en: This also kind of goes along with an exaggerated need for attention and validation, as well as, like, this need to control their relationships,
sentences.zh: 这同时也伴随着对关注和认可的夸大需求，以及控制自己人际关系的欲望，

sentences.en: as well as their work and their own lives.
sentences.zh: 还有控制他们的工作和他们自己的生活。

sentences.en: And I think the three biggest indicators, though, that are, like, firstly, you know, massive red flags in any relationship, but also cause a lot of
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为最显眼的三大指标，它们一方面是任何关系中的巨大危险信号（红线），但同时也引发了大量的

sentences.en: interpersonal conflict and difficulty.
sentences.zh: 人际冲突和困难。

sentences.en: And then these are these three huge red flags related to narcissism and how it presents in people.
sentences.zh: 这就是与自恋及其在人们身上表现相关的三大巨大危险信号。

sentences.en: These are a lack of boundaries.
sentences.zh: 它们分别是：缺乏边界感。

sentences.en: A lack of responsibility for their own actions.
sentences.zh: 不为自己的行为承担责任。

sentences.en: So someone who is a narcissist may always blame outside events or people or emotions for their own actions, which, oh my God, I can relate to.
sentences.zh: 所以一个自恋的人总是会把自己的行为归咎于外部事件、他人或情绪，哦天哪，对此我简直感同身受。

sentences.en: That was just like this person I used to date.
sentences.zh: 这就像我以前约会过的那个人一样。

sentences.en: And any time I'd be like, oh, you know, probably shouldn't have treated me like that, probably shouldn't have said that, didn't really appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 每当我想要说，噢，你知道的，你大概不该那样对待我，大概不该说那些话，我真的很不高兴时，

sentences.en: They'd be like, oh, you know, it's just because of this that's happened and it's because I've, because I'm suffering, it's because of my emotions,
sentences.zh: 他们就会说，噢，你知道的，这只是因为发生了这样那样的事，是因为我在受苦，是因为我的情绪，

sentences.en: like, it has nothing to do with you, has nothing to do with me not caring about you.
sentences.zh: 这跟你一点关系也没有，跟我是不是不在乎你也毫无关系。

sentences.en: It has everything to do with external events.
sentences.zh: 这全都是因为外部事件造成的。

sentences.en: And finally, a big red flag and a big thing that narcissists often show is just a general lack of empathy.
sentences.zh: 最后，一个巨大的危险信号以及自恋狂经常表现出的重大特征，就是普遍缺乏同理心。

sentences.en: Yeah, like I said, like the lack of responsibility was a big, big one for me that I think I saw in this person that I used to date.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像我说的，缺乏责任感对我来说是一个非常非常深刻的感受，我想我在我曾经约会过的这个人身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, anytime they did something wrong and were confronted with this, they could never see the hurt that that would cause and would constantly blame these external events,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每当他们做了错事并面对质问时，他们永远看不到这会造成怎样的伤害，并会不断把责任归咎于外部事件，

sentences.en: particularly like uni and stress and housing situation.
sentences.zh: 特别是像大学学业、压力和住房状况之类的。

sentences.en: So they just were unable to be held accountable for how they treated others.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们根本无法为自己如何对待他人承担责任。

sentences.en: There was also always like an urgency to make things right so that they could redeem themselves as the good guy rather than like actually taking real and honest responsibility
sentences.zh: 而且他们总是急于把事情弄好，好让自己重塑“好人”的形象，而不是真正诚实地为自己的行为承担真正的责任。

sentences.en: for their actions.
sentences.zh: 对于他们的行为。
